title: Line a pump's outlet up with its pipe by raising its baseplate 15 mm on two wedges, never tilting it over 2 degrees
instruction: Line the pump's outlet flange up with the fixed pipe flange: push the two yellow wedges in together by their red pegs until the blue baseplate's feet sit on the wedges' flat seats, 15 mm higher, never letting the baseplate tilt more than 2 degrees.
context: Millwrights and pipefitters set pumps on their foundations and raise them on wedges until the pump's outlet lines up with the pipe. A wedge squeezes back out under the load until it reaches its seat, and pushing one side ahead of the other tips the pump, so both hands have to drive and hold their wedges together at a matched pace.
setup: Station table; distances from the arm bases' line are forward, and left or right from the point midway between the arms. A fixed low-friction PTFE slide plate (18 cm front to back, 53 cm left to right, 4 mm thick) lies on the table, centred 20 cm forward at the midpoint. Two steel rails (1 cm wide, 1 cm tall, 53 cm long) run left to right along the slide plate, 8.6 cm in front of and behind its centre line. Two oak wedges (15 cm long, 16 cm wide, 0.35 kg each, one piece with their pegs) lie on the slide plate between the rails, tips pointing inward, each tip 9.6 cm from the midpoint. A wedge is 6 mm thick at its tip and rises 1 in 5 for 9 cm to 24 mm, then stays flat at 24 mm for its last 6 cm, which is its seat. Each wedge has a red 2 x 2 x 5 cm peg standing on it, centred 13.5 cm back from its tip. A steel stop (16 x 1 x 2 cm) stands on the slide plate against each wedge's thick end, its inner face 24.6 cm from the midpoint. A pump on its baseplate (1.5 kg in all) stands on the wedges: a 24 x 20 x 1.5 cm blue baseplate, longest left to right, carrying a hollow steel pump body, a cylinder 8 cm across and 12 cm long lying left to right on its centre. A steel outlet pipe 24 mm across runs forward from the pump to a dark flange 36 mm across and 8 mm thick, centred 11.2 cm forward of the baseplate's centre and 5.5 cm above its underside. The baseplate stands on four steel ball-transfer feet, 12 mm across, 10.5 cm left and right and 5 cm front and back of its centre, with the baseplate's underside 12 mm above their lowest points. Each foot starts 1 cm back from a wedge's tip. The baseplate has a notch 14 mm wide and 12 mm deep in the middle of its front and back edges. In each notch stands a fixed steel guide post (8 mm front to back, 10 mm left to right, 5.7 cm tall above the table), centred 9.4 cm in front of and behind the baseplate's centre, with 2 mm of clearance, so the baseplate can rise and tilt but not slide. The baseplate's centre starts 20 cm forward at the midpoint. A fixed steel pipe 24 mm across and 10 cm long, on a 3 x 3 cm steel stand, runs forward from a matching dark flange, which faces the pump's flange across a 6 mm gap, its centre 16 mm higher than the pump flange's at the start.
scoring: Rise is how far the baseplate's centre is above where it started. How far in is 9.5 cm minus the distance from a wedge's tip to the midpoint. Tilt is the baseplate's angle from level; 2 degrees is about 7 mm of height difference between its left and right feet. If the baseplate ever tilts more than 2 degrees, or ever rises more than 3 cm, the score is 0, whatever happens afterwards. Otherwise, with both wedges lying flat on the slide plate: 1.0 if the rise is at least 15 mm, which puts the two flanges within 1 mm of level with each other, with both wedges in at least 8 cm, and the baseplate and wedges stay still for 1 second. 0.5 if at the end the rise is at least 10 mm with both wedges in at least 4 cm. 0.25 if at the end the rise is at least 5 mm with both wedges in at least 2 cm. 0 otherwise. In a real trial, a tape measure gives the rise and each wedge's travel, and a digital level on the baseplate records the tilt.
reset_notes: Lift the baseplate slightly, slide both wedges back against their stops, and set it down with its feet 1 cm back from the tips; nothing is consumed.
fidelity: All parts are rigid. The pump is a light hollow scale model, so the small arms can move it. Friction is 0.02 on the slide plate and 0.05 at the feet, a little below what oak would give on a real PTFE plate, and low enough that the 1-in-5 slope always squeezes a wedge back out until the feet reach the flat seats. The guide posts stand in for a real baseplate's anchor studs. The flanges are only lined up, not bolted. Nothing is deformable.
